name: Yulan Guo

papers.title: Trust-Calibrated VLA Policy Post-Training with Evolving Imagination
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are often pretrained via imitation learning, making post-training with reinforcement learning (RL) important once deployment moves beyond demonstration coverage. Existing VLA-RL paradigms expose a reliability--efficiency tension. Model-free refinement avoids simulator bias but is costly, static model-based refinement improves efficiency with stale imagination, and online-updated model-based refinement adapts the simulator without auditing generated rollouts. We propose Model-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (MERL), a trust-calibrated framework for VLA policy post-training with simulator-generated imagination. MERL couples policy optimization with an evolving simulator composed of a world model and a reward proxy head, and calibrates imagined rollouts through two-level trust rather than using them uniformly. Across training stages, MERL adjusts the imagined-data ratio and rollout horizon according to simulator reliability; within generated rollouts, it selects and weights reliable imagined chunks before policy optimization. This mechanism keeps refinement close to real-data-driven policy improvement when the simulator is unreliable, and increases the influence of imagination as reliability improves. Experiments on long-horizon perturbed manipulation tasks show that MERL improves final success rate and online learning efficiency over imitation learning, model-free RL, and static or online-updated model-based baselines.

papers.title: PAWN: Preference-Aware Semantic NFT for Online Reinforcement Learning of Flow-based VLAs
papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning for flow-based manipulation policies is challenging because multi-step solver-based action generation makes the action likelihoods required by standard policy-ratio objectives difficult to access. Hopefully, NFT-style methods offer a promising likelihood-free route for local policy optimization, and recent embodied extensions have begun to adapt this idea to flow-based robot policies. However, several structural issues remain: trajectory-level outcomes provide noisy and misaligned credit for action chunks and their intermediate solver states; full-space mirrored comparisons ignore the compositional geometry of robot actions; and local updates may still follow noisy behavior-sampled continuations without explicitly identifying better alternatives, which may be guided toward the manifold of suboptimal actions. We present Preference-Aware Semantic NFT (PAWN), a unified NFT-style online RL framework that addresses these issues through structured local preference optimization. PAWN derives implicit chunk-level preference signals by lifting solver-step density comparisons to chunk-path scores, reorganizes mirrored local evidence into SE(3)-aware motion modes, and uses conditional pair guidance to favor locally better continuations. Experiments on flow-based manipulation benchmarks show consistent gains in adaptation efficiency, final success, and OOD robustness over strong online RL baselines.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Absolute Pose Regression via Geometric Pose Proxy
papers.abstract: Absolute pose regression (APR) provides an attractive route to real-time camera relocalization through a single feed-forward pass. However, the image-to-pose formulation hides the perspective and scene geometries that make localization well constrained, limiting its accuracy. To address this mismatch, we reformulate APR as a geometry-aware regression pipeline. The query image is first lifted into a scene pointmap, providing the downstream regressor with a geometric representation rather than appearance-only features. We then introduce a Gram-based pose proxy inspired by classical absolute pose estimation, where the network predicts a structured Gram matrix that jointly encodes perspective constraints and scene geometry. During training, we further propose geometry-guided pointmap augmentation, which constructs additional samples at novel viewpoints directly in the pointmap space. Compared with novel-view-synthesis-enhanced APR, it provides more geometry-focused samples without costly rendering or training an additional neural scene representation. Indoor and outdoor experiments show that our method substantially improves accuracy while retaining efficient feed-forward inference, achieving a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
